summary: Partial extraction of generic GL3 Serre weights, numerical Breuil–Mézard, cosocle lattices and Breuil lattice locality. The full main-paper text has been read. This checkpoint resolves the graph/lattice proof spine, separates the main geometry and patching endpoints, verifies concrete library carriers, routes reusable local algebra to its existing owners, and proposes two additional layers without a patching/lattice cycle. Original prerequisite proofs, many local charts and a complete definition/key-theorem inventory remain unclosed; see G01–G09. Continuation #1402 adds the absolute Hartogs and flat-base-change proof interfaces, distinguishes ordinary spectra from formal deformation notation, and supplies the torsion-free specialization algebra. It corrects the interior extension-graph degree to 7|J|. All 84 earlier item IDs and 39 earlier source-issue IDs are retained; global duality, chart and original-input gaps remain.

conventions.coefficients: p>3; E/Q_p finite and sufficiently large for all embeddings, tame types and constituent fields of definition; O its integers, varpi a uniformizer, F its residue field. p and varpi are distinct symbols. Finite O-module means finitely generated, not necessarily torsion. Unless explicitly specified, type rings impose parallel Hodge–Tate weights eta=(2,1,0), with cyclotomic character of weight +1.
conventions.local: K_v/Q_p is unramified in the main numerical/GL3 assertions; k_v has p^f_v elements and J is the disjoint union of its embeddings, f=sum f_v. Distinguish the algebraic restriction-of-scalars GL3 group, its finite group of rational points, and G1T. Genericity is measured via lowest-alcove presentations and D01; the complete construction is G01. Semisimplicity of a Galois representation is an independent hypothesis, not implied by inertial genericity.
conventions.notation: sigma(tau)^sigma denotes the O-lattice with irreducible residual cosocle sigma, not a power. Rbar means reduction modulo varpi. Graph arrows run from quotient to subobject. Radical grades start at zero; soc_-1=0. The lattice exponent in Theorem 4.1.9(5) is a power of p after unramified descent, even if E is ramified.

global.field: F/F+ is CM with F+≠Q; F/F+ is unramified at every finite place, p is unramified in F+, and each p-place of F+ splits in F. Fix a lift v-tilde in F of every relevant split place.
global.group: G/F+ is the definite unitary outer form of GL3 used in §5.3: compact at every real place and quasi-split at finite places, split by F. Fix the integral model and split-place identifications iota_v with GL3(O_Fv). Construction/existence is G07.
global.residual: The continuous residual rbar is automorphic, has split ramification and satisfies D21; at all p-places it is semisimple, and at the chosen lifts it is 10-generic. Automorphic means nonzero localized finite-level algebraic automorphic forms for some coefficients; level lowering supplies the fixed minimal choices below.
global.level: Choose the auxiliary place v1 as in CEG+16 §2.3 (exact selection conditions remain G07). U^p is hyperspecial at split v≠v1, the inverse image of upper triangular matrices at v1, and hyperspecial at inert v. Sigma0 contains precisely the ramified away-p places. W is a fixed O-lattice in the product of their minimal types as in CHT08 Definition 2.4.14, whose detailed definition remains G07.
global.hecke: Use the paper’s dual convention: det(1−rbar^dual(Frob_w)X)=sum_(j=0)^3 (−1)^j Norm(w)^(j(j−1)/2) alpha(T_w^(j)) X^j. m is the kernel of alpha; lambda is the characteristic-zero eigensystem of the lift. Keep the distinguished v1 Hecke operator and omitted finite places as in §5.3.
global.lift: For T48/T49, r is continuous, absolutely irreducible, almost everywhere unramified, r^c≅r^dual epsilon^−2, potentially crystalline of type ((2,1,0),tau_v) at chosen p-places, with the residual automorphic K-type condition of T48. T49 additionally requires a 13-generic tame p-type and minimal ramification away from p in the exact CHT sense. The conclusion is locality up to homothety.

items.name: Representation carrier
items.statement: For a semiring k and monoid G, Rep k G bundles an additive commutative group V, a k-module structure and a monoid representation on V; morphisms are equivariant linear maps. Finite-dimensionality and continuity are additional restrictions.

items.statement: For any ring A and A-module M, socle A M is the supremum of its simple submodules; it is semisimple and contains every semisimple submodule.

items.statement: Let R be commutative, M an R-module, N a finitely generated submodule and I an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of zero. If N ≤ I N, then N=0. Apply to a finite cokernel to lift generators.

items.name: Depth in a p-alcove
items.statement: Fix p>3, X*(T)=(Z^3)^J and eta=(2,1,0)^J. A weight is n-deep in an alcove if, for every positive coroot alpha with alcove strip mp< <lambda+eta,alpha> <(m+1)p, its pairing lies strictly between mp+n and (m+1)p−n.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Keep all positive coroots, strict inequalities, and embedding coordinates; affine p-dot translations are by p times a weight.
items.proofOutline: Keep all positive coroots, strict inequalities, and embedding coordinates; affine p-dot translations are by p times a weight.

api.name: depth_affine_invariant

api.name: depth_mono
api.statement: n-depth implies m-depth for 0≤m≤n.

unitTests: A weight on a strip endpoint is not 0-deep.
For p=101 the triple (40,20,0) is 13-deep in C0 after adding eta.

items.name: Extension graph
items.statement: For p-regular Serre weights of GL3(k) with a fixed central character, use the injective translation charts Tr_mu of §2.1. In coordinates (omega,a) in Lambda_W × {0,1}^J, two vertices are adjacent iff exactly one embedding changes, its label flips, and the weight-coordinate difference is 0, ±epsilon1, ±epsilon2 or ±(epsilon1−epsilon2). Chart overlap transports this relation.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Translation-map construction and overlap proofs are explicit remaining gaps G01; the graph must not be defined by Ext, whose comparison is a theorem.
items.proofOutline: Translation-map construction and overlap proofs are explicit remaining gaps G01; the graph must not be defined by Ext, whose comparison is a theorem.

items.name: Graph distance
items.statement: For the extension graph within a fixed central-character component, d_gph is the length of a shortest edge path. The component is connected; on a product of embedding graphs this distance is the sum of component distances.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Prove connectivity before exporting an N-valued metric; an arbitrary graph distance can be infinite.
items.proofOutline: Prove connectivity before exporting an N-valued metric; an arbitrary graph distance can be infinite.

items.name: Nine-point constituent model
items.statement: For one embedding define Sigma with lower-label points 0, epsilon1, epsilon2, epsilon1+epsilon2, epsilon1−epsilon2, epsilon2−epsilon1 and upper-label points 0, epsilon1, epsilon2. Sigma_inn is the three lower points 0,epsilon1,epsilon2; Sigma_obv is its complement. For J take products; r flips every alcove label.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Use the actual finite coordinate set; compare it with constituents by Proposition 2.3.5, not by definition.
items.proofOutline: Use the actual finite coordinate set; compare it with constituents by Proposition 2.3.5, not by definition.

unitTests: One factor has six obvious and three inner points.

items.name: Defect
items.statement: For a generic Deligne–Lusztig R and its constituent chart Sigma^J, Def_R(sigma) is the number of embeddings at which its coordinate lies in Sigma_inn.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. The chart comparison and the constituent bijection must be supplied by G01; do not count all lower-alcove coordinates as inner.

api.statement: 0≤Def≤|J|.

unitTests: (epsilon1+epsilon2,0) has defect zero.

items.name: Graph bipartiteness
items.statement: The extension graph is bipartite by the parity of the number of upper labels, so an edge changes distance from a fixed vertex by an odd number, necessarily ±1.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Each edge flips precisely one label. Triangle inequalities bound the change by one.
items.proofOutline: Each edge flips precisely one label. Triangle inequalities bound the change by one.

items.name: Longest geodesics and defect descent
items.statement: In the nine-point product graph, every vertex kappa lies on a geodesic from sigma to a vertex at distance D=3|J|−Def(sigma). Every farthest vertex has defect at most Def(sigma). If both defects equal a positive delta, there is a neighbor of the farthest vertex with defect delta−1 and distance D−1 from sigma.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Prove one nine-point factor by enumeration and extend using sums. Executed finite checks for |J|=1,2 are evidence, not a proof for arbitrary products.
items.proofOutline: Prove one nine-point factor by enumeration and extend using sums. Executed finite checks for |J|=1,2 are evidence, not a proof for arbitrary products.

items.name: Radical and cosocle
items.statement: For a nonzero finite-length object M of a finite abelian F-category, rad(M) is the smallest subobject whose quotient is semisimple; cosoc(M)=M/rad(M). For a finite-dimensional algebra this is the intersection of maximal submodules.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Establish existence through finite length; use the module presentation and L02 for the dual socle construction.
items.proofOutline: Establish existence through finite length; use the module presentation and L02 for the dual socle construction.

api.name: cosoc_right_exact
api.statement: Cosocles preserve epimorphisms and induced quotient radical filtrations.

api.name: radical_semisimple_quotient
api.statement: M/rad(M) is semisimple and universal among semisimple quotients.

unitTests: A simple object has zero radical.
The length-two Jordan block for F[t]/t^2 has one-dimensional radical and cosocle.
For S⊕T the radical is zero.

items.name: Radical filtration
items.statement: For finite-length M, set rad^0 M=M and rad^(n+1) M=rad(rad^n M), with decreasing semisimple associated grades rad^n/rad^(n+1).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Termination uses finite length. Transport across quotient maps to prove strict compatibility, needed by Q_sigma.
items.proofOutline: Termination uses finite length. Transport across quotient maps to prove strict compatibility, needed by Q_sigma.

api.name: rad_zero
api.statement: rad^0 M=M.

api.name: rad_quotient
api.statement: A quotient receives its radical filtration from M.

unitTests: For a simple object only grade zero survives.
For F[t]/t^3 the three grades are at 0,1,2.
The quotient by t^2 of that module has length two.

items.name: Socle filtration
items.statement: For finite-length M, set soc_-1 M=0; soc_n M is the inverse image of soc(M/soc_(n−1) M). Its semisimple grade n is soc_n/soc_(n−1).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Reuse TauCeti.socle on module presentations and prove transport to finite abelian categories; no second socle carrier.
items.proofOutline: Reuse TauCeti.socle on module presentations and prove transport to finite abelian categories; no second socle carrier.

api.name: socle_grade_zero
api.statement: The grade at zero is soc(M).

api.name: socle_subobject
api.statement: A subobject receives the socle filtration by intersections.

unitTests: For S simple, soc_0 S=S.
For F[t]/t^3, soc_0=(t^2), soc_1=(t).
The zero subobject has every socle term zero.

items.name: Loewy length and rigidity
items.statement: For nonzero finite-length M, its Loewy length ell is the common termination length of its radical and socle filtrations, with last nonzero grade ell−1. It is rigid iff rad^n M=soc_(ell−n−1) M for 0≤n≤ell.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. First prove that the two lengths coincide and are minimal among lengths of exhaustive separated semisimple filtrations. The definition does not assert every module is rigid.
items.proofOutline: First prove that the two lengths coincide and are minimal among lengths of exhaustive separated semisimple filtrations. The definition does not assert every module is rigid.

api.name: loewy_minimal
api.statement: Every semisimple filtration has length at least ell.

api.name: rigid_grades
api.statement: Rigid modules have opposite radical/socle grades.

unitTests: A simple object has ell=1 and is rigid.
F[t]/t^3 has ell=3 and is rigid.
S⊕F[t]/t^2 has ell=2 and is not rigid: its radical omits the direct simple summand in soc_0.

items.name: Multiplicity-free extension digraph
items.statement: For multiplicity-free finite-length M, vertices are its simple composition factors. Put sigma→sigma_prime iff M has a nonsplit length-two subquotient 0→sigma_prime→E→sigma→0. A subset is closed when it contains every target of every arrow out of it.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Direction is from quotient to subobject. Multiplicity-freeness is essential for the reconstruction theorem; use composition-factor sets only after proving it.
items.proofOutline: Direction is from quotient to subobject. Multiplicity-freeness is essential for the reconstruction theorem; use composition-factor sets only after proving it.

api.name: extension_arrow
api.statement: An arrow produces the specified nonsplit exact sequence.

api.name: closed_intersection
api.statement: Intersections of closed vertex sets are closed.

unitTests: For a split sum S⊕T the two-vertex graph has no edges.
A nonsplit extension of S by T has arrow S→T.
S⊕S is rejected as not multiplicity free.

items.name: Subobjects are closed constituent subsets
items.statement: For multiplicity-free M in a finite abelian category, N↦JH(N) bijects subobjects of M with closed subsets of its extension digraph.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. For surjectivity take a minimal subobject containing the chosen factors; an extra factor maximal in the arrow order would give a removable simple quotient. For injectivity multiplicity-freeness identifies intersections by their factors.
items.proofOutline: For surjectivity take a minimal subobject containing the chosen factors; an extra factor maximal in the arrow order would give a removable simple quotient. For injectivity multiplicity-freeness identifies intersections by their factors.

items.name: Filtered extension graph and depth
items.statement: For a semisimple exhaustive separated filtration F of a multiplicity-free object M, d_F(sigma) is its unique nonzero associated-grade index. Gamma_F retains arrows for which the induced shifted filtration on the length-two extension has length two; radical and socle graphs use their respective filtrations.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Require semisimple filtration for the Hom-to-grade definition; for arbitrary grades a factor need not be in the socle of its grade. The semisimple hypothesis is necessary for the Hom-based degree definition; see E16.
items.proofOutline: Require semisimple filtration for the Hom-to-grade definition; for arbitrary grades a factor need not be in the socle of its grade.

api.name: filtered_arrow_grades
api.statement: A filtered arrow relates consecutive relevant grades.

api.name: subquotient_full_graph
api.statement: Subquotients inherit the full digraph on their vertices and the restricted filtration.

unitTests: The nonsplit length-two extension has depths 0 and 1 for the radical filtration.
The same extension reverses depth order under the socle filtration.
A split sum has no filtered arrows even if placed in distinct grades.

items.name: Paths in Loewy filtrations
items.statement: For multiplicity-free M, every constituent in radical grade n is the end of a radical extension path of length n; dually every constituent in socle grade n starts a socle path of length n.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Successively select a nonsplit extension with a factor in the adjacent grade; otherwise that factor would split off earlier.
items.proofOutline: Successively select a nonsplit extension with a factor in the adjacent grade; otherwise that factor would split off earlier.

items.name: Rigidity by continuing extension paths
items.statement: For multiplicity-free M of Loewy length ell, rigidity is equivalent to each sigma starting a radical extension path of length ell−1−d_rad(sigma); equivalently each sigma ends a socle path of length ell−1−d_soc(sigma).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Arrow paths bound the opposite filtration depth from below; equation (4.1) gives the reverse inequality. Equality for every factor gives equality of subobjects via multiplicity-freeness.
items.proofOutline: Arrow paths bound the opposite filtration depth from below; equation (4.1) gives the reverse inequality. Equality for every factor gives equality of subobjects via multiplicity-freeness.

items.name: Duality reverses extension arrows
items.statement: An exact contravariant duality on a finite abelian category sends a multiplicity-free object to one with the opposite extension digraph, and reverses extension paths and radical/socle filtrations.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Dualise 0→T→E→S→0 to 0→S*→E*→T*→0. Both unrestricted and filtered graphs require transposition.
items.proofOutline: Dualise 0→T→E→S→0 to 0→S*→E*→T*→0. Both unrestricted and filtered graphs require transposition.

items.name: Irreducible-cosocle lattices
items.statement: For a 2-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation R of the product of GL3(k_v) over a sufficiently large finite p-adic coefficient field E, each sigma∈JH(R) has an O-stable lattice R^sigma with cosocle of its reduction isomorphic to sigma, unique up to homothety.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. The original EGS15 §4.1 proof was read: residual multiplicity-freeness gives existence and uniqueness of the cosocle lattice up to homothety. The Deligne–Lusztig multiplicity-free input and unramified coefficient descent remain G02.
items.proofOutline: The original EGS15 §4.1 proof was read: residual multiplicity-freeness gives existence and uniqueness of the cosocle lattice up to homothety. The Deligne–Lusztig multiplicity-free input and unramified coefficient descent remain G02.

items.name: Normalised saturated inclusion
items.statement: For full O-lattices Lambda2⊂Lambda1 in one finite-dimensional E-vector space, the inclusion is saturated in this paper’s sense iff Lambda2 is not contained in varpi Lambda1, equivalently its reduction map is nonzero.
items.locator: Definition 4.3.4 and Remark 4.3.5; normalization condition in EGS15 Lemma 4.1.2
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. This normalisation is not the usual torsion-free-cokernel usage of saturated submodule. For two full lattices that latter condition would force equality.
items.proofOutline: This normalisation is not the usual torsion-free-cokernel usage of saturated submodule. For two full lattices that latter condition would force equality.

api.name: normalise_inclusion
api.statement: A unique integral power of varpi normalises an inclusion between two lattice homothety representatives.

api.name: reduction_nonzero
api.statement: Normalisation is equivalent to a nonzero reduction map.

unitTests: pO⊕O⊂O^2 is normalised although its cokernel is torsion.
pO^2⊂O^2 is not normalised when O is unramified.
O^2⊂O^2 is normalised.

items.name: Saturation distance
items.statement: For the lattices R^sigma of a 3-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation, first normalise R^kappa⊂R^sigma. Define d_sat(sigma,kappa) to be the unique nonnegative integer d for which p^d R^sigma⊂R^kappa is normalised.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Existence of an integral exponent of p, rather than merely varpi, uses descent of R and its cosocle lattices to an unramified coefficient field; prove that descent in G02.
items.proofOutline: Existence of an integral exponent of p, rather than merely varpi, uses descent of R and its cosocle lattices to an unramified coefficient field; prove that descent in G02.

api.name: sat_independent
api.statement: The integer is independent of homothetic choices.

api.name: sat_ramified_base_change
api.statement: Extending coefficients preserves the p-exponent.

unitTests: For O^2 and pO⊕O over unramified O, the distance is one.
After adjoining a ramified uniformizer, the distance remains one in p-units.
The distance from a lattice class to itself is zero.

items.name: Saturation distance is a metric
items.statement: On JH(R) in D14, d_sat is symmetric, vanishes exactly on equal constituents, and satisfies the triangle inequality.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Use chains p^a L⊂M⊂L and p^b M⊂N⊂M; composition bounds d(L,N) by a+b. Symmetry follows by exchanging endpoints and scaling. Zero gives equal lattice classes, hence equal cosocles.
items.proofOutline: Use chains p^a L⊂M⊂L and p^b M⊂N⊂M; composition bounds d(L,N) by a+b. Symmetry follows by exchanging endpoints and scaling. Zero gives equal lattice classes, hence equal cosocles.

items.name: Minimal constituent submodule
items.statement: For sigma,sigma1∈JH(R), Q_sigma(sigma1) is the unique minimal submodule of Rbar^sigma containing sigma1. It is the image of any nonzero map Rbar^sigma1→Rbar^sigma and has cosocle sigma1.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Use multiplicity-freeness: any quotient by a submodule containing sigma1 has no sigma1 factor, so the image of the sigma1-cosocle module maps to zero there.
items.proofOutline: Use multiplicity-freeness: any quotient by a submodule containing sigma1 has no sigma1 factor, so the image of the sigma1-cosocle module maps to zero there.

api.name: minimal_factor
api.statement: Q is contained in every submodule containing sigma1.

api.name: image_normalised
api.statement: The image of a normalised lattice map is Q.

unitTests: Q_sigma(sigma)=Rbar^sigma.
In S→T, Q(T)=T and Q(S)=M.
A zero morphism is excluded from the image characterisation.

items.name: Radical depth inequality for Q
items.statement: If sigma2∈JH(Q_sigma(sigma1)), then d_rad^sigma(sigma2)≥d_rad^sigma(sigma1)+d_rad^sigma1(sigma2). Its grade within Q is exactly d_rad^sigma1(sigma2).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. The surjection from Rbar^sigma1 strictly preserves radical filtrations; restriction of the shifted filtration from Rbar^sigma gives the inequality. Radical depth has not yet been proved a metric.
items.proofOutline: The surjection from Rbar^sigma1 strictly preserves radical filtrations; restriction of the shifted filtration from Rbar^sigma gives the inequality. Radical depth has not yet been proved a metric.

items.name: Extensions are graph edges
items.statement: For p-regular Serre weights sigma=F(mu) and kappa, with mu 6-deep componentwise and within the §4.2 GL3 setup, Ext^1_G(kappa,sigma) is nonzero iff d_gph(sigma,kappa)=1; then its F-dimension is one.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Use Q1(mu)|G=Inj(F(mu)), compute its first socle layer by translation (4.9) and compare weights via (4.10). This needs Frobenius-kernel injectives, Jantzen/Pillen and the translation theorem: G03.
items.proofOutline: Use Q1(mu)|G=Inj(F(mu)), compute its first socle layer by translation (4.9) and compare weights via (4.10). This needs Frobenius-kernel injectives, Jantzen/Pillen and the translation theorem: G03.

items.name: Graph distance bounds radical depth
items.statement: If R is 6-deep, d_gph(sigma,kappa)≤d_rad^sigma(kappa) for constituents of R.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. A radical path to kappa has one graph edge at each step by T09. Visual inspection of arXiv p.72 and published p.99 confirms that the displayed Ext group is NONZERO; a missing negation in extracted text is an OCR artefact, not a source issue.

items.name: Normal-crossing shape chart
items.statement: For semisimple 10-generic residual GL3 data and a nonzero tame type with every shape component of length at least two, the explicit chart is formally smooth over R_N=completed tensor_j O[[x_j,y_j]]/(x_j y_j−p), where N=sum_i(4−length(w_i)). Each weight prime chooses one variable from every pair, together with varpi.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. LLHLM18 explicit rings are G04. Keep formal variables and coefficient ramification; reducedness holds modulo varpi, not automatically modulo p.
items.proofOutline: LLHLM18 explicit rings are G04. Keep formal variables and coefficient ramification; reducedness holds modulo varpi, not automatically modulo p.

items.name: Component prime distance
items.statement: In T11, the chosen-variable sets for sigma and kappa differ in 2 d_gph(sigma,kappa) elements. The sum of the two primes has height d_gph(sigma,kappa)+1 in the mixed-characteristic chart.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Use Table 3 component matching and tensor factorisation; two set elements change for each variable-pair flip. This is a sum of ideals, not a set intersection.
items.proofOutline: Use Table 3 component matching and tensor factorisation; two set elements change for each variable-pair flip. This is a sum of ideals, not a set intersection.

items.name: Adjacent weights have saturation distance one
items.statement: For a 13-generic R and sigma1,sigma2∈JH(R) with graph distance one, d_sat(sigma1,sigma2)=1.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Globalise to semisimple 10-generic local data containing both weights and with shape lengths ≥2; choose a weak minimal patching functor. Descend to S=Z_p[[(x_j,y_j),t]]/(x_j y_j−p), whose special fibre is reduced. After normalising p^k R1⊂R2⊂R1, component annihilators force y2^2…yN^2 M(sigma1)⊂y1…yN M(sigma1) if k>1. Freeness over F[[y1,…,yN,t]] contradicts that divisibility. Requires G04/G05; this is not a purely finite-group proof.
items.proofOutline: Globalise to semisimple 10-generic local data containing both weights and with shape lengths ≥2; choose a weak minimal patching functor. Descend to S=Z_p[[(x_j,y_j),t]]/(x_j y_j−p), whose special fibre is reduced. After normalising p^k R1⊂R2⊂R1, component annihilators force y2^2…yN^2 M(sigma1)⊂y1…yN M(sigma1) if k>1. Freeness over F[[y1,…,yN,t]] contradicts that divisibility. Requires G04/G05; this is not a purely finite-group proof.

items.name: Saturation is bounded by graph distance
items.statement: For 13-generic R, d_sat(sigma,kappa)≤d_gph(sigma,kappa).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Sum the adjacent-weight equality along a shortest path using the metric triangle inequality.
items.proofOutline: Sum the adjacent-weight equality along a shortest path using the metric triangle inequality.

items.name: Adjacent normalised lattices are comparable
items.statement: For 13-generic R and graph-adjacent sigma1,sigma2, normalised embeddings R^sigma_i⊂R^sigma have comparable images.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Write p^(k+1)R1⊂R2⊂p^k R1 using T13. Normalisation against the common target gives −1≤k≤0.
items.proofOutline: Write p^(k+1)R1⊂R2⊂p^k R1 using T13. Normalisation against the common target gives −1≤k≤0.

items.name: Radical depth orients lattice inclusions
items.statement: Under T15, if d_rad^sigma(sigma2)≥d_rad^sigma(sigma1), then R^sigma2⊂R^sigma1.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. The opposite containment would put Q_sigma(sigma1) inside Q_sigma(sigma2), contradicting T08.
items.proofOutline: The opposite containment would put Q_sigma(sigma1) inside Q_sigma(sigma2), contradicting T08.

items.name: Predicted radical strata
items.statement: For 2-generic R, the radical strata of Rbar^sigma are predicted when d_rad^sigma(kappa)=d_gph(sigma,kappa) for every constituent kappa.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. This is weaker a priori than recovering all extension arrows.
items.proofOutline: This is weaker a priori than recovering all extension arrows.

api.name: predicted_strata_grade
api.statement: The grade n has exactly the factors at graph distance n.

api.name: strata_to_edges
api.statement: Under 13-genericity, predicted strata imply the predicted radical graph.

unitTests: At distance zero the only constituent is sigma.
A factor at distance one must be in grade one.
A filtration with the right length but a misplaced factor fails the predicate.

items.name: Strata determine the radical graph
items.statement: If R is 13-generic and the radical strata from sigma are predicted, then Gamma_rad(Rbar^sigma) has exactly the edges kappa1→kappa2 with d_gph(kappa1,kappa2)=1 and d_gph(sigma,kappa2)=d_gph(sigma,kappa1)+1.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. T16 places the next-depth factor inside Q; T08 forces its relative depth to be one. Conversely a radical edge is a graph edge by T09.
items.proofOutline: T16 places the next-depth factor inside Q; T08 forces its relative depth to be one. Conversely a radical edge is a graph edge by T09.

items.name: Maximally saturated constituent
items.statement: For 13-generic R, sigma is maximally saturated if every kappa at maximal graph distance D=3f−Def_R(sigma), with f=|J|, has d_sat(sigma,kappa)=D.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Quantify over every farthest constituent; positive defect can give more than one.
items.proofOutline: Quantify over every farthest constituent; positive defect can give more than one.

api.name: maximal_sat_all_distances
api.statement: Maximal saturation implies equality of graph and saturation distance to every constituent.

api.name: maximal_sat_defect_zero
api.statement: The unique opposite weight suffices at defect zero.

unitTests: In one factor an inner vertex has eccentricity two.
An obvious lower vertex has eccentricity three.
Checking only one farthest vertex is insufficient when several exist.

items.name: Maximal saturation controls all distances
items.statement: For 13-generic R, sigma is maximally saturated iff d_sat(sigma,kappa)=d_gph(sigma,kappa) for every kappa.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Extend a geodesic through kappa to a farthest vertex by T02. The triangle inequality for d_sat and upper bound T14 sandwich both partial distances to equality.
items.proofOutline: Extend a geodesic through kappa to a farthest vertex by T02. The triangle inequality for d_sat and upper bound T14 sandwich both partial distances to equality.

items.name: Radical paths give lattice chains
items.statement: For 13-generic R, normalise all cosocle lattices inside R^sigma. A radical extension path starting at sigma gives a nested chain R^sigma_d⊂…⊂R^sigma_1⊂R^sigma.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Each adjacent pair has increasing radical depth, so apply T16. Consecutive and endpoint inclusions retain the specified normalisation.
items.proofOutline: Each adjacent pair has increasing radical depth, so apply T16. Consecutive and endpoint inclusions retain the specified normalisation.

items.name: Maximal saturation predicts radical strata
items.statement: For 13-generic R, if sigma is maximally saturated, every radical depth equals graph distance, and the radical graph is predicted.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. If a radical path has length k exceeding endpoint distance, its first failure to increase distance drops by two relative to its index, by bipartiteness. T19 then sandwiches the corresponding lattice between R^sigma and p^(i−1)R^sigma, contradicting distance i from T18.
items.proofOutline: If a radical path has length k exceeding endpoint distance, its first failure to increase distance drops by two relative to its index, by bipartiteness. T19 then sandwiches the corresponding lattice between R^sigma and p^(i−1)R^sigma, contradicting distance i from T18.

items.name: Lower-alcove defect-zero base case
items.statement: For 13-generic R and a lower-alcove constituent sigma of defect zero, the radical strata and both extension graphs of Rbar^sigma are predicted and Rbar^sigma is rigid.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Embed Rbar^sigma uniquely up to scalar into the multiplicity-free U⊂V_mu|G of Theorem 4.2.7(3); use equality of the 9^f factors and the full-subgraph property. Constructing U and its arrows requires all of §4.2.7–4.2.15 and original algebraic representation theory; G03 remains open.
items.proofOutline: Embed Rbar^sigma uniquely up to scalar into the multiplicity-free U⊂V_mu|G of Theorem 4.2.7(3); use equality of the 9^f factors and the full-subgraph property. Constructing U and its arrows requires all of §4.2.7–4.2.15 and original algebraic representation theory; G03 remains open.

items.name: Lower-alcove base case is maximally saturated
items.statement: For 13-generic R, a lower-alcove defect-zero sigma is maximally saturated.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Apply T21 to R and its dual; use opposite radical paths to obtain a strictly decreasing chain of integral p-exponents of length 3f. Thus d_sat to the unique opposite weight is at least 3f; T14 gives equality.
items.proofOutline: Apply T21 to R and its dual; use opposite radical paths to obtain a strictly decreasing chain of integral p-exponents of length 3f. Thus d_sat to the unique opposite weight is at least 3f; T14 gives equality.

items.name: Every defect-zero constituent is maximally saturated
items.statement: For 13-generic R, any sigma with Def_R(sigma)=0 is maximally saturated.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Propagate T22 along the connected obvious-weight graph. For adjacent obvious weights compare the two opposite geodesics; failure of either outer lattice inclusion to be normalised would force radical depth at least 3f+1 where T20 gives 3f−1.
items.proofOutline: Propagate T22 along the connected obvious-weight graph. For adjacent obvious weights compare the two opposite geodesics; failure of either outer lattice inclusion to be normalised would force radical depth at least 3f+1 where T20 gives 3f−1.

items.name: All constituents are maximally saturated
items.statement: For 13-generic R every constituent is maximally saturated.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Induct on defect. For a farthest constituent of lower defect use symmetry and T18. For equal positive defect use T02 to select a neighbor of defect one less. T15 gives two lattice-containment cases. In the first, a hypothetical shorter saturation exponent forces a Q-depth at least d+1 instead of d−1. In the second, reverse the long radical path from that neighbor and use the first bipartite distance drop as in T20.
items.proofOutline: Induct on defect. For a farthest constituent of lower defect use symmetry and T18. For equal positive defect use T02 to select a neighbor of defect one less. T15 gives two lattice-containment cases. In the first, a hypothetical shorter saturation exponent forces a Q-depth at least d+1 instead of d−1. In the second, reverse the long radical path from that neighbor and use the first bipartite distance drop as in T20.

items.name: Graph distance equals radical depth
items.statement: For a 13-generic Deligne–Lusztig R for the product of GL3(k_v), every sigma,kappa∈JH(R) satisfies d_rad^sigma(kappa)=d_gph(sigma,kappa).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. T24 plus T20. No generalisation to nongeneric types or arbitrary groups is claimed.
items.proofOutline: T24 plus T20. No generalisation to nongeneric types or arbitrary groups is claimed.

items.name: Loewy-length formula
items.statement: Under T25, ell(Rbar^sigma)=2 Def_R(sigma)+3(f−Def_R(sigma))+1=3f−Def_R(sigma)+1, f=sum_v[k_v:F_p].
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Take maximum radical depth using T02, then add one for zero-based grades.
items.proofOutline: Take maximum radical depth using T02, then add one for zero-based grades.

items.name: Predicted radical extension graph
items.statement: For 13-generic R and sigma, Gamma_rad(Rbar^sigma) consists of graph edges oriented away from sigma.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Apply T17 to T25.
items.proofOutline: Apply T17 to T25.

items.name: Predicted full extension graph
items.statement: For 13-generic R and sigma, the full Gamma(Rbar^sigma) is the graph with the same vertices and graph edges oriented away from sigma.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. T27 supplies every outward edge. T09 permits only graph edges. A reversed edge would create a two-cycle, impossible for the extension graph of a multiplicity-free finite-length object.
items.proofOutline: T27 supplies every outward edge. T09 permits only graph edges. A reversed edge would create a two-cycle, impossible for the extension graph of a multiplicity-free finite-length object.

items.name: Rigidity of cosocle-lattice reduction
items.statement: For 13-generic R every Rbar^sigma is rigid.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Every directed path extends to maximum possible length using the product model T02; apply T05 to T25 and T27.
items.proofOutline: Every directed path extends to maximum possible length using the product model T02; apply T05 to T25 and T27.

items.name: Normalised p-power lattice inclusion
items.statement: For 13-generic R and a normalised inclusion R^kappa⊂R^sigma, p^d R^sigma⊂R^kappa is normalised for d=d_gph(kappa,sigma).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. T24 and T18 identify d_sat with graph distance. The exponent is of p; replacing it with varpi changes the assertion after ramified coefficient extension.
items.proofOutline: T24 and T18 identify d_sat with graph distance. The exponent is of p; replacing it with varpi changes the assertion after ramified coefficient extension.

items.name: Reduced equidimensional surjection criterion
items.statement: Let S→R be a surjective homomorphism of Noetherian equidimensional rings of the same finite Krull dimension d. Assume S is reduced and S,R have the same finite number of minimal primes. Then the map is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Lemma 3.6.11, in its complete Noetherian local application
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Each minimal prime of R pulls back to a minimal prime of S: a strict containment over a minimal prime would reduce dimension. Equality of finite counts makes the pullback set exhaustive. The kernel lies in every minimal prime of S, hence in its zero nilradical. No assertion for arbitrary infinite sets of minimal primes.
items.proofOutline: Each minimal prime of R pulls back to a minimal prime of S: a strict containment over a minimal prime would reduce dimension. Equality of finite counts makes the pullback set exhaustive. The kernel lies in every minimal prime of S, hence in its zero nilradical. No assertion for arbitrary infinite sets of minimal primes.

items.name: Four-prime monomial quotient
items.statement: For any field F, F[[a,b,c,d,e,f]]/(ab,ac,ae,bc,bd,cf) is reduced and equidimensional of dimension three, with minimal primes (a,b,c),(a,b,f),(a,c,d),(b,c,e).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. The ideal equals the intersection of the four coordinate ideals: a monomial is in each iff its support hits each of the four variable triples, equivalently it is divisible by one listed degree-two generator. Each prime quotient is a three-variable power-series domain. The same monomial-support test applies to series coefficientwise. Minimal-prime enumeration independently executed.
items.proofOutline: The ideal equals the intersection of the four coordinate ideals: a monomial is in each iff its support hits each of the four variable triples, equivalently it is divisible by one listed degree-two generator. Each prime quotient is a three-variable power-series domain. The same monomial-support test applies to series coefficientwise. Minimal-prime enumeration independently executed.

items.name: Identity-shape triple intersection
items.statement: In the identity-shape special-fibre ring of §3.6 with semisimple 10-generic residual data, set w0=c_(0,0)∩c_(0,1). Then w0∩c_(epsilon1,0)∩c_(epsilon2,0)=(c22,c33).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Set all three unit parameters equal to one, as permitted by the source formal-power-series decomposition. Eliminate c11 and set a=c12−c13 c32, b=kappa c31−c21 c32, c=c23, d=c13, e=c21, f=c32, where kappa is the nonzero scalar of the source presentation (published p.70). The resulting quotient has ideal (ab,ac,ae,bc,bd,cf), so T32 proves reducedness, dimension three and four minimal primes. Apply T31 to the surjection onto the intersection quotient. The full chart presentation and its coefficient calculation remain G04.
items.proofOutline: Set all three unit parameters equal to one, as permitted by the source formal-power-series decomposition. Eliminate c11 and set a=c12−c13 c32, b=kappa c31−c21 c32, c=c23, d=c13, e=c21, f=c32, where kappa is the nonzero scalar of the source presentation (published p.70). The resulting quotient has ideal (ab,ac,ae,bc,bd,cf), so T32 proves reducedness, dimension three and four minimal primes. Apply T31 to the surjection onto the intersection quotient. The full chart presentation and its coefficient calculation remain G04.

items.name: Weak minimal patching functor
items.statement: For a finite set S of p-adic fields K_v, residual rho_v:G_Kv→GL3(F), and R_infty=(completed tensor_v R^square_rho_v)[[x1,…,xh]], let X_infty=Spf R_infty. A weak minimal patching functor is a nonzero covariant exact functor from continuous K=product_v GL3(O_Kv) representations on finite O-modules to coherent X_infty-modules. It sends each tame-type lattice to a p-torsion-free maximal Cohen–Macaulay module over R_infty(tau); if M_infty(R_1(mu)) is nonzero then each rho_v has a semistable lift of type tau_v(1,mu_v); each Serre weight maps to zero or an MCM module of pure special-fibre dimension d; after inverting p, each type-lattice module has rank at most one on each connected component of its type space.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Keep this arithmetic functor distinct from the already-owned abstract inverse-limit patching construction R03.5. Its global existence is G05.
items.proofOutline: Keep this arithmetic functor distinct from the already-owned abstract inverse-limit patching construction R03.5. Its global existence is G05.

api.name: patch_exact
api.statement: Short exact sequences of finite K-modules remain exact.

api.name: patch_type_mcm
api.statement: A type lattice maps to a p-torsion-free MCM module.

api.name: patch_rank_bound
api.statement: Generic component rank is at most one.

unitTests: The zero functor is excluded.
A nonzero MCM module on just one component is not automatically faithful.
A patching functor must preserve the nonsplit length-two exact sequence used in 5.1.5.

items.name: Fixed-dimension Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity
items.statement: Fix d from the dimension d+1 of a nonempty type space. For finite M supported in dimension at most d, e_d(M) is d! times the degree-d coefficient of its Hilbert–Samuel polynomial, so it is zero if dim Supp(M)<d.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Develop the Hilbert polynomial and additivity under R03.3; do not use the usual multiplicity in the module’s own dimension for every M.
items.proofOutline: Develop the Hilbert polynomial and additivity under R03.3; do not use the usual multiplicity in the module’s own dimension for every M.

api.name: multiplicity_low_dimension
api.statement: Support dimension below d implies e_d=0.

api.name: multiplicity_exact
api.statement: e_d is additive in finite short exact sequences.

unitTests: A finite-length module contributes zero when d>0.
For d=0 the invariant is its length.
For an exact sequence of equal-dimensional modules the leading coefficients add.

items.name: Numerical Breuil–Mézard for weak minimal patching
items.statement: Suppose every K_v/Q_p is unramified and every rho_v is semisimple and 10-generic. For any weak minimal patching functor, e_d(M_infty(sigma)) equals 1 for sigma∈W?(rho_S), and 0 otherwise.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Eliminate extraneous weights via generic lifts and §2.3.13; descend positive defect by the difference 2^(delta+1)−2^delta; propagate from an obvious weight using §3.5.9–12. The full type construction and weight recipe remain G01/G04/G05.
items.proofOutline: Eliminate extraneous weights via generic lifts and §2.3.13; descend positive defect by the difference 2^(delta+1)−2^delta; propagate from an obvious weight using §3.5.9–12. The full type construction and weight recipe remain G01/G04/G05.

items.name: Weight support is predicted
items.statement: Under T34, W_BM(rho_S)=W?(rho_S), independently of the choice of weak minimal patching functor.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Use the pure-dimensional MCM axiom: a nonzero weight module has positive dimension-d multiplicity, so multiplicity zero cannot conceal a nonzero lower-dimensional module.
items.proofOutline: Use the pure-dimensional MCM axiom: a nonzero weight module has positive dimension-d multiplicity, so multiplicity zero cannot conceal a nonzero lower-dimensional module.

items.name: Non-generic type emptiness
items.statement: For K/Q_p unramified and rho:G_K→GL3(F) semisimple and 10-generic, R^tau_rho=0 if the tame type tau is not 1-generic.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Uses Enns weight elimination; original theorem and proof are G04.
items.proofOutline: Uses Enns weight elimination; original theorem and proof are G04.

items.name: Nonzero type ring is a normal domain
items.statement: For unramified K/Q_p, continuous semisimple 10-generic rho:G_K→GL3(F), and a 1-generic tame type tau with R^tau_rho≠0, the complete framed potentially crystalline ring of Hodge type (2,1,0) is a normal domain.
items.locator: Theorem 3.5.3, normal-domain assertion with E04 nonzero qualification
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. The proof explicitly treats nonzero rings and matches them with reduced equidimensional explicit charts using multiplicities. The zero ring is not a domain. Do not infer normality merely from special-fibre reducedness.
items.proofOutline: The proof explicitly treats nonzero rings and matches them with reduced equidimensional explicit charts using multiplicities. The zero ring is not a domain. Do not infer normality merely from special-fibre reducedness.

items.name: Canonical component labeling
items.statement: For semisimple 10-generic rho over unramified K, there is a unique assignment sigma↦p(sigma) of predicted weights to primes in R^square_rho such that for each tame type tau the special fibre of R^tau_rho is the reduced union of components labeled by W?(rho,tau).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Start with defect-zero types selecting individual primes and use the unique minimal type at each higher defect; no arbitrary independent bijection for each type.
items.proofOutline: Start with defect-zero types selecting individual primes and use the unique minimal type at each higher defect; no arbitrary independent bijection for each type.

items.name: Patching support respects component labels
items.statement: For finite unramified semisimple 10-generic local data and any weak minimal patching functor, the scheme-theoretic support of M_infty(tensor_v sigma_v) for predicted sigma_v is Spec R_infty/(sum_v p(sigma_v)R_infty).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Use exactness, reduced type support and induction on defect; the primes do not depend on the globalization or patching choices.
items.proofOutline: Use exactness, reduced type support and induction on defect; the primes do not depend on the globalization or patching choices.

items.name: Upper-alcove condition gives rank-one freeness
items.statement: In §5.1, assume rho_S is semisimple 10-generic over unramified fields, M_infty is weak minimal, tau_S is 13-generic with R_infty(tau_S)≠0, and sigma=F(lambda)∈W?(rho_S,tau_S). If lambda_(pi^−1(i)) is in upper alcove C1 whenever length(w_i*)≤1, then M_infty(sigma(tau_S)^sigma) is free of rank one over R_infty(tau_S).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Five cyclicity steps 5.1.3–7: normal-crossing base case, four-point fiber-product gluing, six-point extension, eight-point gluing, all-nine extension. Ideal identities 3.6.12–16 and EGS15 Lemma 10.1.13 are required. Lift generators by Nakayama; a nonzero cyclic MCM module with full support over a domain is faithful and hence free. Full gluing contracts remain G06.
items.proofOutline: Five cyclicity steps 5.1.3–7: normal-crossing base case, four-point fiber-product gluing, six-point extension, eight-point gluing, all-nine extension. Ideal identities 3.6.12–16 and EGS15 Lemma 10.1.13 are required. Lift generators by Nakayama; a nonzero cyclic MCM module with full support over a domain is faithful and hence free. Full gluing contracts remain G06.

items.name: Lower-alcove short-shape obstruction
items.statement: With the same §5.1 hypotheses and sigma∈W?(rho_S,tau_S), if for some i the shape length is ≤1 and lambda_(pi^−1(i)) lies in C0, then M_infty(sigma(tau_S)^sigma) is not free over R_infty(tau_S).
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. The source gives a proof sketch: embed into the free module of a suitable upper-alcove constituent, identify the image ideal by component intersections, and show its residual minimal-generator space has dimension >1. Completion/radicality and every Table 3 generator calculation remain G06.
items.proofOutline: The source gives a proof sketch: embed into the free module of a suitable upper-alcove constituent, identify the image ideal by component intersections, and show its residual minimal-generator space has dimension >1. Completion/radicality and every Table 3 generator calculation remain G06.

items.name: Codimension-two complement for gauges
items.statement: For the nonzero normal type scheme X=Spec R_infty(tau_S) under §5.1 hypotheses, let Z be the union of intersections of distinct components of X_F and j:U=X\Z→X. Every point of the crossing locus has height at least two in X; the locus may be empty.

items.name: Regularity away from crossings
items.statement: For U in D20, U is regular.

items.name: Gauge on the regular open
items.statement: Under §5.2 hypotheses, for a normalised injection iota:sigma(tau_S)^kappa→sigma(tau_S)^sigma, let m(theta) be the composition multiplicity of theta in its finite torsion cokernel. On U the image of M_infty(iota) equals (product_theta p(theta)^m(theta)) times M_infty(sigma(tau_S)^sigma), restricted to U.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. On U both patched modules are line bundles by MCM regular-local freeness. Their quotient gives a Cartier divisor whose coefficients are the lengths at the corresponding special-fibre components.
items.proofOutline: On U both patched modules are line bundles by MCM regular-local freeness. Their quotient gives a Cartier divisor whose coefficients are the lengths at the corresponding special-fibre components.

items.name: Global gauge ideal
items.statement: In T43 additionally assume sigma satisfies the upper-alcove condition of T40. Then the image of M_infty(iota) is [j_* j^*(product_theta p(theta)^m(theta) R_infty(tau_S))] M_infty(sigma(tau_S)^sigma).
items.note: Absolute total-space Hartogs argument supplied in this continuation; global arithmetic prerequisites remain open.
items.proofOutline: The source module of the injected patching map is full-support MCM, so T58 extends it uniquely from U. T43 computes that restriction as the product ideal times the target. T40 makes the target free of rank one, and T61 converts extension of its product submodule to the embedded Hartogs ideal. The initial product ideal itself need not be MCM.

items.name: Gauge ideal descends to local data
items.statement: The ideal in T44 is obtained by base change from the completed tensor product of the local potentially crystalline rings, hence from an ideal in the tensor product of unrestricted framed local deformation rings.
items.note: No comparison between open subsets of adic Spf and ordinary Spec is needed: coherent patched modules are used as finite modules over the same complete rings. Completion must not be substituted for ordinary localization on U.
items.proofOutline: Set A=completed tensor_v R_v^tau, B=A[[x_1,…,x_h]], and use ordinary Spec A and Spec B. T62 identifies the crossing opens. The weight-prime product is extended from A. A is normal CM in the source setup, so A→sections(U_A,O) is an isomorphism by T58. T60 identifies the two embedded Hartogs ideals. Pull back this finite ideal through the surjection from the completed tensor of unrestricted framed rings.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles condition in this paper
items.statement: For residual r:G_F→GL3(Fcoef), require that its image contain GL3(F0) for some subfield F0⊂Fcoef with |F0|>9, and that the field fixed by ker(ad r) does not contain F(zeta_p).

items.name: Global Serre weights
items.statement: Use the definite unitary global setup specified in conventions.global: CM F/F+, F+≠Q, unramified at finite places, p unramified in F+ and split in F, split residual ramification, fixed minimal away-p level and coefficients. If r is automorphic, satisfies D21, and each chosen local rho_v is semisimple and 10-generic, then its weights at that level equal W?(rho_S), with the fixed identifications iota_v.

items.name: Mod-p multiplicity one
items.statement: In the global setup of T46, choose 13-generic tau_S and sigma satisfying all hypotheses and the upper-alcove short-shape condition of T40. The m-eigenspace of S(U^pG(O_F+,p),(sigma(tau_S)^sigma reduced modulo varpi composed with product iota_v)^dual tensor W_Sigma0 reduced modulo varpi) has F-dimension one.

items.proofOutline: Equation (5.8) is dual to the residue of a free rank-one patched module. The condition is not restricted to all-upper weights, nor true for arbitrary weights; use T40’s exact conditional bound.

items.name: Automorphy lifting
items.statement: In the global setup, let r:G_F→GL3(E) be continuous and absolutely irreducible, unramified almost everywhere, with r^c≅r^dual epsilon^−2. Assume its residual representation satisfies D21 and split ramification, is semisimple at all p-places and 10-generic there; for each chosen p-place r is potentially crystalline of parallel Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0) and tame type tau_v. Suppose rbar is the residual representation of a RACSDC automorphic representation pi of GL3(A_F) with trivial infinitesimal character and with product sigma(tau_v) as its local K-type. Then r is automorphic.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Uses T37 connected generic fibres and T46 in the proof of LLHLM18 Theorem 7.4. The source cross-reference must still be expanded with its corrected level-lowering argument; G07.
items.proofOutline: Uses T37 connected generic fibres and T46 in the proof of LLHLM18 Theorem 7.4. The source cross-reference must still be expanded with its corrected level-lowering argument; G07.

items.name: Breuil lattice locality
items.statement: Let r satisfy all hypotheses of T48 and additionally be minimally ramified away from p in the sense of CHT08 Definition 2.4.14. For its 13-generic tame p-type tau_S, the integral lattice cut out in sigma(tau_S) by the completed automorphic eigenspace S-tilde(U^p,W)[lambda] depends, up to homothety, only on the local representations {r|G_Kv}_v.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Choose a T40 cosocle lattice; express the automorphic lattice as sum_kappa gamma(kappa)^−1 sigma(tau)^kappa by EGS15 Lemma 4.1.2. Schikhof duality identifies (gamma(kappa)) with the image of the specialised patched map. T44–45 show each ideal is local. Integral torsion-free specialisation and the exact CHT minimal condition are unresolved G02/G07/G08. This is an abstract locality theorem, not a complete explicit Dieudonne formula.
items.proofOutline: Choose a T40 cosocle lattice; express the automorphic lattice as sum_kappa gamma(kappa)^−1 sigma(tau)^kappa by EGS15 Lemma 4.1.2. Schikhof duality identifies (gamma(kappa)) with the image of the specialised patched map. T44–45 show each ideal is local. Integral torsion-free specialisation and the exact CHT minimal condition are unresolved G02/G07/G08. This is an abstract locality theorem, not a complete explicit Dieudonne formula. Apply T63 to the patched inclusion after choosing the free target. Exactness of patching transports a coefficient-power annihilator of the finite lattice quotient to the module cokernel. The specialized image ideal is correct after removing O-torsion; the raw source need not be O. The global Schikhof comparison is still G07/G08.

items.statement: For Noetherian A, ideal I and finite M, depth_I(M) is the supremum of lengths of M-regular sequences in I, with value infinity when IM=M. For local A, depth(M) uses its maximal ideal. M is Cohen–Macaulay if depth(M)=dim Supp(M), and maximal Cohen–Macaulay if depth(M)=dim A. Full support means Supp(M)=Spec A and is a separate condition.

items.name: Sections on a finite union of principal opens
items.statement: Let A be commutative, I=(f_1,…,f_r), U=Spec A minus V(I), and M an A-module. Define Sec_U(M)=Gamma(U,M-tilde). By the sheaf axiom it is the kernel of product_i M[f_i^−1]→product_(i<j) M[(f_i f_j)^−1], whose (i,j)-component is the difference of the two restrictions. The empty cover has zero sections.

items.statement: Let A→O be a ring map to a DVR and M a finite A-module. Set M_O^tf=(M tensor_A O)/T, where T consists of elements killed by a nonzero element of O. This is specialization followed by the torsion-free quotient; it is not generally the raw tensor product.

items.name: Flat base change for sections on an open
items.statement: Let A→B be flat, U⊂Spec A quasi-compact open and M an A-module. Then Sec_U(M) tensor_A B→Sec_(U_B)(M tensor_A B) is an isomorphism, where U_B is the inverse image open in Spec B.

Localization commutes with tensor. These identifications also identify the restriction maps, so this is the canonical base-change map. No properness or formal-scheme theorem is needed.

These identifications also identify the restriction maps, so this is the canonical base-change map. No properness or formal-scheme theorem is needed.

items.name: Local-cohomology restriction exact sequence
items.statement: For Noetherian A, ideal I, U=Spec A minus V(I), and A-module M, the Ext-colimit local cohomology of L06 fits functorially into 0→H_I^0(M)→M→Sec_U(M)→H_I^1(M)→0.

For Noetherian A this agrees with support cohomology (0955). The augmented finite localization Čech complex computes that support functor (0952/0A6T). Its first two cohomology groups are the kernel and cokernel of M→Sec_U(M). The Noetherian comparison is essential, not a theorem already provided by L06.
items.proofOutline: Compare the Ext colimit with derived I-power torsion using an injective resolution and exact filtered colimits. For Noetherian A this agrees with support cohomology (0955). The augmented finite localization Čech complex computes that support functor (0952/0A6T). Its first two cohomology groups are the kernel and cokernel of M→Sec_U(M). items.name: Depth two annihilates the first local cohomology groups
items.statement: For Noetherian A, finite M and ideal I, if depth_I(M)≥2 then H_I^0(M)=H_I^1(M)=0. If IM=M both groups also vanish.

Pass to the Ext colimit. Equivalently use the regular-element induction in 47.11.1. If IM=M, finite generation gives support disjoint from V(I), so these groups vanish.
items.proofOutline: A regular sequence in I of length two gives Ext_A^q(A/I^n,M)=0 for q<2 for every n, using equality of depth for I and I^n. Pass to the Ext colimit. Equivalently use the regular-element induction in 47.11.1. If IM=M, finite generation gives support disjoint from V(I), so these groups vanish.

items.name: Full-support Cohen–Macaulay modules localize with full depth
items.statement: For Noetherian local A and finite Cohen–Macaulay M with Supp(M)=Spec A, every localization M_P has depth_A_P(M_P)=dim A_P. In particular its depth is at least two at primes of height at least two.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. CM localizes by 10.103.11. Support localizes to all of Spec A_P by the full-support assumption. Thus the CM depth equals dim A_P. This supplies the stalkwise condition and avoids the false inference from MCM to support on every component in general.
items.proofOutline: CM localizes by 10.103.11. Support localizes to all of Spec A_P by the full-support assumption. Thus the CM depth equals dim A_P. This supplies the stalkwise condition and avoids the false inference from MCM to support on every component in general.

items.name: Absolute Hartogs extension for a full-support MCM module
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian local ring, M finite Cohen–Macaulay with full support, and Z⊂Spec A closed with every point of height at least two. For j:U=Spec A minus Z→Spec A, M-tilde→j_*j^*M-tilde is an isomorphism. The conclusion also holds for any coherent sheaf on a locally Noetherian scheme whose stalks have depth at least two on the complement.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. By T57 every removed stalk has depth at least two. On each affine neighborhood T65 and T56 give vanishing in degrees zero and one, and T55 identifies the restriction as an isomorphism. These maps are natural and glue. This uses absolute stalk depths; the relative fibrewise codimension condition in HK04 3.5 is not asserted for the special-fibre crossings.
items.proofOutline: By T57 every removed stalk has depth at least two. On each affine neighborhood T65 and T56 give vanishing in degrees zero and one, and T55 identifies the restriction as an isomorphism. These maps are natural and glue. This uses absolute stalk depths; the relative fibrewise codimension condition in HK04 3.5 is not asserted for the special-fibre crossings.

items.name: Coherent ideal extension from the Hartogs open
items.statement: Under D24, H_U(J) is a finite ideal of A, its associated sheaf is j_*(J-tilde|U), and it restricts to J-tilde on U. If J-tilde has depth at least two on the complement, H_U(J)=J.
items.locator: LLHLM20 gauge ideal; Stacks0E9I and quasi-compact-open quasi-coherence

As a submodule of Noetherian A it is finite. For the final assertion apply absolute Hartogs to J-tilde. Do not claim an arbitrary initial product ideal is already MCM.

items.name: Hartogs ideal closure commutes with flat scalar extension
items.statement: Let A→B be flat between Noetherian rings, let U⊂Spec A be quasi-compact and assume A≅Sec_U(A). For J⊂A, B≅Sec_(U_B)(B) canonically and H_U(J)B=H_(U_B)(JB) as embedded ideals of B.

The comparison is compatible with both inclusions into B. This proves equality of ideals, not merely an abstract module isomorphism.

items.name: Hartogs extension and a finite free target
items.statement: Let A,U satisfy D24, J⊂A and L a finite free A-module. Then j_*j^*(J L) is canonically H_U(J) tensor_A L inside L-tilde. For rank one this is H_U(J)L and is independent of the chosen basis of L.

Naturality under GL(L) makes the isomorphism independent of basis. In rank one rescaling the generator by a unit preserves the embedded ideal.
items.proofOutline: After a basis choice both sides are finite direct sums of the same ideal-section module; the equalizer commutes with finite sums. Naturality under GL(L) makes the isomorphism independent of basis. In rank one rescaling the generator by a unit preserves the embedded ideal.

items.name: Crossing opens pull back under adjoining formal variables
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian complete local over a DVR O, A/varpi reduced, and let P_i⊂A be the inverse images of the finitely many minimal primes of A/varpi. Put B=A[[t_1,…,t_h]]. The minimal primes of B/varpi are P_i B/varpi. For Z_A=union_(i<j) V(P_i+P_j), its inverse image in Spec B is the crossing locus Z_B of the special fibre. Hence U_B=Spec B minus Z_B is the inverse image of U_A. All spectra here are ordinary spectra of the complete rings.
items.locator: LLHLM20 §5.2 setup and Remark5.2.4, with Spf notation made explicit
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. A→B is flat and finite intersections extend under a flat map. Each quotient B/P_iB=(A/P_i)[[t]] is a domain. Since the intersection of the P_i modulo varpi is zero, these extended primes are exactly the minimal primes. The ideals of pairwise intersections extend to their sums. The paper has precisely B=A[[x_1,…,x_h]] for the type quotient; no general equivalence of open subsets of Spec and Spf is claimed.
items.proofOutline: A→B is flat and finite intersections extend under a flat map. Each quotient B/P_iB=(A/P_i)[[t]] is a domain. Since the intersection of the P_i modulo varpi is zero, these extended primes are exactly the minimal primes. The ideals of pairwise intersections extend to their sums. items.name: DVR specialization of a lattice image
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian, pi∈A, u:M→A an injection from a finite module, and I=im(u), with pi^n A⊂I for some n. Let a:A→O be a map to a DVR with a(pi) nonzero. The induced map M tensor_A O→O has image IO and torsion kernel; it identifies M_O^tf with the nonzero ideal IO. Thus M_O^tf is free of rank one even when the raw specialization has torsion.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. After inverting pi, u becomes an isomorphism because its cokernel is killed by pi^n. After tensoring with Frac(O) it remains an isomorphism. Consequently the specialized kernel is O-torsion, and every torsion element maps to zero in O, so the kernel is exactly the torsion submodule. Right exactness gives image IO, containing a(pi)^n. A nonzero ideal of a DVR is free of rank one. This does not supply the separately required Schikhof-duality identification of the automorphic lattice.

items.name: Stalkwise depth two gives a regular pair on the support ideal
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian, M finite, I an ideal, and suppose depth(M_P)≥2 for every P∈V(I) in Supp(M). If IM≠M then I contains an M-regular sequence of length two. If IM=M use the infinite-depth convention.
